# API reference

Only when the source has API or endpoint docs. Skip this for pure content sites.

## Find or build the spec

1. **Use the source's spec.** Look for an OpenAPI file in the repo, a download link on the reference pages, or common paths (`/openapi.json`, `/swagger.json`, `/api-docs`). A spec in the repo or export is the source of truth for operations (`mint migrate --topic discovery`, Get the source); never edit it to match the old site's rendered output. Platforms that render a playground usually embed the spec or a fragment per operation in the page source; extract and merge them (dedupe `components.schemas`, union `tags`).
2. **Only if no spec exists**, and the user agrees, build one from the reference pages. Every path, parameter, field, type and example must come from the source. Mark the result in the report as reconstructed.

One spec per product, stored at `openapi/<product>.json` or `.yaml`. Do not merge unrelated APIs or split one API across files. A usable spec has `info`, `servers` with the real base URL, `security` with matching `components.securitySchemes`, `tags` with descriptions, and per operation: `operationId`, `summary`, parameters, request body and at least one success response with an example.

If the platform changed the spec at build time (decorators, overrides, overlays), bake those changes into the spec or port them to an OpenAPI Overlay referenced as `"openapi": { "source": "...", "overlays": ["..."] }`. Otherwise readers lose them.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/api-playground/openapi-setup.md

## Choose how pages render

- **Source has generated reference pages** (one page per operation, little extra prose): add a group with the spec and let Mintlify generate the pages.

  ```json
  { "group": "API reference", "openapi": "openapi/core.json" }
  ```

- **Source has hand-written page per endpoint with real prose** (common on hosted platforms): migrate each page as normal and add the operation to its frontmatter, so the page keeps its prose and gains the playground at its original URL.

  ```mdx
  ---
  title: 'List loads'
  openapi: 'GET /v1/loads'
  ---
  ```

  With several specs, qualify it: `openapi: "openapi/core.json GET /v1/loads"`. Method and path must match the spec exactly.

Never do both for the same operations. That publishes every endpoint at two URLs.

Add root-level `api` config so the playground and code samples render:

```json
"api": {
  "playground": { "display": "interactive" },
  "examples": { "languages": ["curl", "python", "javascript"] }
}
```

Only enable `interactive` if the source's API accepts browser requests the user is happy to expose; otherwise use `"simple"`.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/settings-api.md

## Code samples

When the source shows per-language samples for an operation, add them to that operation in the spec as `x-codeSamples` entries so they render in the request panel. Use a snippet in the endpoint page only when a sample needs surrounding prose or repeats across many endpoints. Never invent samples.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/api-playground/adding-sdk-examples.md

## Generated URLs

Never predict generated page paths. Run `mint dev`, read each generated endpoint page's path from its sidebar link or URL, and use those for links and redirect destinations. Then run `mint broken-links` to catch any link or redirect that points at a page that does not exist. Paths come from the tag name and operation `summary`, lowercased with spaces turned into `-` and only `{}(),.'/` removed, so a tag like `[Integrations] AWS` becomes `[integrations]-aws`.

If the source URLs differ from the generated ones, set `x-mint: { href: "<old path>" }` on each operation to keep its old URL, or add `redirects` from each old endpoint URL (from the old sitemap). If tag names produce ugly slugs, tell the user rather than renaming tags silently, since tags may be shared with their SDK tooling.

## Pages that dump spec JSON

Some exports render each operation as a heading plus a large `openapi` JSON block. Once the spec is wired in, replace those blocks with a `<CardGroup cols={2}>` of cards linking to the generated pages (title from `summary`, body `` `METHOD /path` ``). Keep the page's intro prose.

## Supporting pages

Migrate overview, authentication, errors, rate limits, pagination, webhooks and SDK pages as normal content pages and list them in the API section of navigation.

Never write SDK or CLI reference content from memory. Every method, field and signature must come from the source docs or the SDK's code.

## Check

- Each spec is referenced from `docs.json`, and every `openapi` frontmatter value resolves to an operation. `mint validate` reports both.
- Open one generated or overlaid page per spec in `mint dev` and confirm method, path, auth and a code sample render.
- No spec file in `openapi/` is unreferenced.
